From Human Markets to Machine Markets: Feedback Stability, Auditable Memory, and Financial Constraints Pratik Niroula ∗ and Prashant Niroula † October 6, 2026 — revision candidate Abstract Aggregate price–flow data reveal model-dependent feedback diagnostics rather than trader identities. In a reset linear cohort model, symmetric near-coincident rates re- quire bounded-power probing budgets of order δ −4 ; a separate scalar Gaussian exper- iment yields a finite-window abstention layer. Reanalysis of recorded Coinbase data shows substantial sensitivity to flow timing and price filtering, while covariance re- strictions are rejected. Saved Binance fee contrasts do not establish a causal response or equivalence. Finally, a declared loss operator and shock set yield an exact budget radius; fixed-spectrum and funded-dealer simulations distinguish transient magnifica- tion from persistent-flow accumulation. Independent replication and policy validation remain open. Keywords: Adaptive learning, algorithmic trading, financial stability, market microstruc- ture, system identification, non-normal dynamics, Kreiss constant. JEL Classification Codes: G01, G10, G14, C32, C58, D83. ∗ Corresponding author email: pratik.niroula@alumni.harvard.edu. Repository ad- dress reported in the original manuscript (remote contents not verified in this revision): github.com/pratikniroula/machine-markets (Revision baseline: 451fd803c516. This candidate has not been independently replicated). † Email: prashant.niroula@alumni.harvard.edu. Niroula and Niroula 1 From Human Markets to Machine Markets Introduction Electronic trading creates a feedback channel when price changes affect subsequent orders and those orders affect later prices. The existence of this channel does not identify its participant-level source: aggregate flow can reflect adaptive algorithms, order splitting, liq- uidity provision, or common information. Nor does decay of price disturbances establish that a dealer’s loss budget will remain intact. This paper separates these identification and financial-risk questions. Our central question is: what can observable aggregate data establish about feedback, and what additional assumptions are required to turn dynamic stability into a financially mean- ingful loss bound? We combine a linear adaptive-memory model with an audit of observable- state definitions and timing, followed by controlled loss-exposure illustrations. The empirical analysis is deliberately reduced-form. It does not identify artificial-intelligence trading, in- dividual learning rules, or a causal market-maker response from anonymous records. Conditional identification results. Within a reset linear cohort model with known price-impact and anchor parameters, price responses identify merged rate–weight measures rather than the number or identity of cohorts sharing a rate. For a uniformly stable compact family of symmetric split alternatives, bounded-power deterministic probes with Gaussian observation noise face a separation lower bound of order δ −4 . This is a lower bound for the stated experiment, not an attained universal rate for all passive market data. A sepa- rate scalar Gaussian price-surveillance experiment gives an explicit finite-window abstention bound near its unit-root boundary. The observation experiment matters: the scalar result is not asserted for noiselessly observed latent cohort states. Measurement sensitivity. The primary empirical reanalysis uses recorded Coinbase BTC, ETH, and ADA book snapshots and signed executed flow from April 7–19, 2021. A 300-second EMA price deviation is estimated on 10-second bins with only end-bin observed flow. Mean reduced-form feedback is approximately 0.00194, 0.00098, and 0.00062, respec- tively. Forward-bin flow alignment produces larger estimates, while raw-return specifications have feedback intervals spanning zero. These comparisons establish that measurement and timing materially affect the feedback diagnostic. They do not establish an algorithmic learning mechanism. The preserved Binance panel supplies a secondary analysis of 768 saved asset-day es- timates, derived from trade-price klines rather than historical full order books. Its legacy forward-flow estimator has mean Q̂ ≃ 0.00815. The raw Binance archives are not present in the inspected cache, so this revision verifies saved-matrix identities and recomputes in- 1 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets ference from saved estimates without claiming a complete raw-data reproduction. The July 2022 fee intervention has a date-clustered effect interval spanning both signs, and equiva- lence is not established at the illustrative margin. Contradictory joint-venue propagation and unsupported event-study inference are withdrawn. Financially meaningful stability. For fixed economically specified state coordinates, loss operator C, and initial-shock set, the exact loss-budget radius is B/ sup t≥0 ∥CJ t ∥ 2 . The underlying transient-growth mechanism is established in operator theory; our financial use is the explicit mapping from a declared disturbance set to a declared budget. A fixed- spectrum numerical illustration separates transient magnification from eigenvalue decay. A distinct funded-dealer simulation shows persistent-flow accumulation and retains an exoge- nous benchmark matched on long-run variance. Simulation outcomes are conditional on their accounting and calibration, not measurements of actual dealer insolvency. 1.1 Related Literature and Contribution Boundaries Classical microstructure studies price formation, information and order flow (Kyle, 1985; Glosten and Milgrom, 1985; Hasbrouck, 1991). Order splitting and book imbalance can create persistent relations without identifying an adaptive trader (Bouchaud et al., 2004; Cont, Kukanov, and Stoikov, 2014). Funding constraints and inventory exposure connect market liquidity to intermediary fragility (Brunnermeier and Pedersen, 2009; Adrian and Shin, 2010; Greenwood, Landier, and Thesmar, 2015). The realization and transient-growth tools used here build on existing control and nu- merical analysis (Gilbert, 1963; Kreiss, 1962; Spijker, 1991; Trefethen and Embree, 2005). Non-normal financial-network amplification is not a first-use claim: Wang, Sornette, Wu and Lera’s 2024 working paper studies evolving influence networks and subcritical financial instabilities (Wang et al., 2024). Singular mixture models also have assumption-dependent identification rates (Manole and Ho, 2022); our symmetric probing experiment is a specific dynamical testing problem rather than a universal new estimation rate. Our scope differs by specifying an output loss budget, a cohort-response observation experiment, and sensi- tivity of measured price–flow feedback to timing and filtering. We do not claim novelty for the general distinction between asymptotic decay and transient growth, or an independently certified priority for the full framework. 2 Niroula and Niroula 1.2 From Human Markets to Machine Markets Evidence Organization Section 2 states the conditional model results. Section 3 defines actual measurements and their timing. Section 4 reports fresh observable-state diagnostics and clearly separated saved- panel evidence. Section 5 examines dimensional stress regression and model-based loss ex- posure. Section 6 states attribution and replication limits. Section 7 discusses conditional surveillance implications and concludes. 2 Theoretical Model and Identification Boundaries 2.1 Microfoundations of Closed-Loop Price Formation We formalize an electronic financial market sampled at discrete uniform time intervals t ∈ {0, 1, 2, . . . }, where time step ∆ represents the operational sampling frequency (e.g., 1 second). Let p t denote the log mid-price of a traded asset, and let p ∗ t denote the unob- served fundamental value, which evolves as a martingale: p ∗ t+1 = p ∗ t + ξ t+1 , ξ t+1 ∼ i.i.d.(0, σ ξ 2 ). (1) We define the pricing error (displacement from fundamental) as x t ≡ p t − p ∗ t . Dealer Pricing and Kyle Auction Microfoundation. Following the continuous auc- tion framework of Kyle (1985) adapted to discrete quote adjustments (Hasbrouck, 1991; Bouchaud et al., 2004), a competitive, risk-neutral market maker sets quotes to absorb ag- gregate order flow. Total incoming order flow at time t consists of two components: aggregate demand u t submitted by algorithmic trading agents, and exogenous liquidity/hedging noise ε t+1 ∼ i.i.d.(0, σ ε 2 ). In addition, fundamentalist arbitrageurs submit mean-reverting demand −φx t whenever prices deviate from fundamentals. The market maker updates the transaction price according to linear price impact κ > 0: p t+1 − p t = κ (u t − φx t + ε t+1 ) . (2) Subtracting fundamental increment ξ t+1 from both sides yields the pricing error recursion: x t+1 = (1 − κφ)x t + κu t + (κε t+1 − ξ t+1 ) . (3) Defining the direct price persistence parameter a ≡ 1−κφ ∈ [0, 1) and rescaling the combined 3 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets disturbance innovation as w t+1 ≡ κε t+1 − ξ t+1 , we obtain the foundational pricing equation: x t+1 = ax t + κu t + w t+1 , w t+1 ∼ i.i.d.(0, σ w 2 ). (4) When fundamentalist arbitrage is strong (φ → 1/κ), a → 0 and prices immediately reflect fundamentals. When liquidity is thin and arbitrage capital is limited, a approaches unity, reflecting high price persistence. Algorithmic Learning Microfoundations. We consider K heterogeneous cohorts of algorithmic traders. Each cohort i ∈ {1, . . . , K} maintains an internal state variable y i,t ∈ R representing its estimate of price momentum, trend, or fundamental mispricing. We show that two stylized signal-update paradigms—steady-state Kalman filtering and regularized Online Gradient Descent—both reduce locally to the identical linear adaptive recursion. Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 demonstrate that exponential memory decay is not an ad hoc modeling assumption, but rather a common local linear reduction of standard optimal fil- tering and regularized gradient optimization. Merged rates identify aggregate weights, not the count or identities of participants sharing a rate in the reset linear experiment. The symmetric split construction makes the leading response difference quadratic in δ, giving a fourth-order testing lower bound with fixed stability margin and noise/power assumptions. This does not identify dollar allocations, supply an upper bound, or justify a literal ratio of detection horizons between δ = 0.05 and a unit perturbation outside the local family. 2.3 Theorem 2: A Finite-Window Price-Surveillance Bound The following experiment isolates a statistical boundary under passive price observations. Its parameter s is the scalar transition coefficient, distinct from the algebraic index S = a + Q of a general multivariate market. Applying the result to a hidden multivariate market requires a valid observation-law reduction; no such reduction is inferred solely from a common unit-root boundary. In particular, a fully observed noiseless cohort recursion need not admit the common Lebesgue densities assumed by an informal reduction to a scalar price likelihood. 2.4 Theorem 3: Intermediary Solvency and the Kreiss Constant Bound We now confront the fundamental divergence between price stability and financial interme- diary solvency. Spectral radius describes asymptotic decay in the linear approximation. Loss 10 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets exposure additionally depends on the shock set, output operator and finite-time magnifica- tion. The Non-Normal Market Jacobian. Consider the closed-loop Jacobian matrix J from (12). In financial markets, price impact and memory adaptation are asymmetric: order flow directly affects prices through contemporaneous impact κ, while price innovations affect memory through learning rate η. As a result, JJ ⊤ − J ⊤ J ̸ = 0: the closed-loop market Jaco- bian J is generically non-normal under asymmetric price-impact and learning parameters (except on a measure-zero algebraic subvariety). While normal matrices have orthogonal eigenvectors that diagonalize under unitary transformations, non-normal matrices have non- orthogonal (nearly parallel) eigenvectors. Consequently, even when all eigenvalues are strictly inside the unit circle (|λ i (J)| ≤ ρ(J) < 1), matrix powers J t can undergo massive transient amplification before decaying asymptotically as t → ∞ (Trefethen and Embree, 2005). Leveraged Dealer Balance-Sheet Model. Let E 0 be unencumbered equity and 0 < γ ≤ 1 a chosen allocation to a modeled absolute loss/exposure budget. Define B = γE 0 . (24) This budget is not leverage-created capital. A separate margin or leverage allowance re- quires its own balance-sheet rule. Fix state units and an output operator C mapping state disturbance to declared dollar exposures. A single row measures one loss channel; multiple commensurately scaled rows define a vector exposure budget. The homogeneous initial-shock calculation below omits ongoing innovations and describes a stylized budget breach, not a complete stochastic solvency model. Let z t ∈ R n denote the state vector of the closed-loop economy evolving as z t = J t z 0 , and let C ∈ R m×n denote the balance-sheet observation operator that maps the state z t into the declared dollar exposures (one output for a scalar dealer loss): Loss t = ∥Cz t ∥ 2 = ∥CJ t z 0 ∥ 2 . (25) A modeled loss-budget breach occurs if sup t≥0 ∥CJ t z 0 ∥ 2 > B. Theorem 2.6 (Dealer Solvency and the Kreiss Constant Bound). Part 1: By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for operator norms, the maximum loss across all initial shock vectors with ∥z 0 ∥ 2 ≤ r is: sup sup ∥CJ t z 0 ∥ 2 = r · sup ∥CJ t ∥ 2 = r · M C . ∥z 0 ∥ 2 ≤r t≥0 (30) t≥0 Requiring that the worst-case loss does not breach capital buffer B imposes r · M C ≤ B, ∗ which holds if and only if r ≤ B/M C ≡ r exact . Part 2: The lower bound K(J) ≤ sup t≥0 ∥J t ∥ 2 follows directly from the Neumann series P −(t+1) t expansion of the resolvent: for |z| > 1, (zI − J) −1 = ∞ J . Taking norms: t=0 z ∥(zI − J) −1 ∥ 2 ≤ ∞ X t=0 |z| −(t+1) ∥J t ∥ 2 ≤ sup ∥J t ∥ 2 t≥0 ∞ X t=0 |z| −(t+1) = sup t≥0 ∥J t ∥ 2 . |z| − 1 (31) Multiplying both sides by (|z| − 1) and taking the supremum over |z| > 1 yields K(J) ≤ sup t≥0 ∥J t ∥ 2 . The upper bound sup t≥0 ∥J t ∥ 2 ≤ e · n · K(J) is Spijker’s Theorem (Spijker, 1991), which establishes the optimal dimensional constant e · n for the discrete Kreiss matrix 12 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets theorem. Inverting the inequality chain K(J) ≤ M I ≤ e · n · K(J) and multiplying by B immediately yields (28). Part 3: Consider the 2 × 2 family of matrices parameterized by θ > 0:   ρ θ  J θ =  , 0 ρ ρ ∈ (0, 1). (32) The eigenvalues are λ 1 = λ 2 = ρ, so ρ(J θ ) = ρ < 1 for all θ. Computing the t-th power:   ρ t tθρ t−1  . J θ t =  0 ρ t (33) Setting C = [1, 0] and initial shock z 0 = [0, 1] ⊤ , the loss at time t is CJ θ t z 0 = tθρ t−1 . Already ∗ at t = 1, the unit shock z 0 = [0, 1] ⊤ has loss θ, so M C ≥ θ and r exact ≤ B/θ. No continuous- ∗ time approximation to the discrete peak is required. Taking θ → ∞, r exact → 0 while the spectral radius remains frozen at ρ, completing the proof. Remark 2.7 (Interpretation and Coordinates). Part 3 concerns the unrestricted class of stable linear matrices. It does not assert that every Jordan-family coupling has an admissible structural market parameterization. Non-normality alone does not imply a large financially relevant transient: the loss operator and disturbance directions must expose it. Rescaling states changes Euclidean shock balls and transient norms unless the metric is transformed consistently. Fixed physical units or a justified weighted norm are therefore necessary for financial comparisons. Under C = I, B/(enK(J)) is a guaranteed conservative lower bound on the allowable radius; B/K(J) is an upper bound, not a safe gating threshold. For a general output matrix, M C ≤ ∥C∥ 2 enK(J) yields a conservative radius B/(∥C∥ 2 enK(J)). 2.5 Pseudospectral Interpretation For ϵ > 0, define σ ϵ (J) = {z : ∥(zI − J) −1 ∥ 2 ≥ ϵ −1 }, including the spectrum by continuity, and α ϵ (J) = sup z∈σ ϵ (J) |z|. The resolvent form of the Kreiss constant is equivalently α ϵ (J) − 1 . ϵ ϵ>0 K(J) = sup This relates transient growth to pseudospectral protrusion outside the unit disk in a specified norm (Trefethen and Embree, 2005). It is a geometric interpretation of established operator theory, not a measured market contour. We report actual matrix-power output magnification 13 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets in Section 5, with explicit matrices and loss coordinates. 2.6 Multi-Asset Generalization and Cross-Impact Kreiss Inflation Modern market makers operate simultaneously across multiple correlated instruments (e.g., BTC, ETH, and altcoins; or equity index components and ETFs). In multi-asset environ- ments, cross-asset price impact creates additional non-normal coupling. Let x t ∈ R d denote the vector of pricing errors across d traded assets, and let u t ∈ R d denote aggregate order flows. The multi-asset price formation equation is: x t+1 = Ax t + Ku t + w t+1 , (34) where A = diag(a 1 , . . . , a d ) ∈ R d×d collects direct price persistences, and K ∈ R d×d is the cross-asset price impact matrix. In general, K is asymmetric (K ̸ = K ⊤ ): institutional order flow in a benchmark asset (such as BTC or SPY) exerts cross-impact on satellite assets, but the reverse flow produces much smaller reactions. Each asset is traded by adaptive momentum flow with learning rates H = diag(η 1 , . . . , η d ) and feedback gain Q ∈ R d×d : y t+1 = (I − H)y t + Hx t+1 , u t = Qy t . (35) Stacking z t = (x t ⊤ , y t ⊤ ) ⊤ ∈ R 2d , the multi-asset closed-loop Jacobian is:   A KQ  ∈ R 2d×2d . J multi =  HA I − H + HKQ (36) Proposition 2.8 (Cross-Impact Kreiss Inflation and Safe Radius Bound in Directed Net- works). Consider a multi-asset economy with directed block-triangular leader-satellite cross- impact (K 12 = 0, K 21 > 0), diagonal feedback matrices Q ≥ 0, anchor matrices A ≥ 0, adap- tation rates H ∈ (0, 1) d , nonnegative cross-impact K ≥ 0, and a nonzero portfolio output op- erator C ≥ 0. Assume ρ(J multi ) < 1. Let J diag denote the decoupled Jacobian where K 21 = 0. The directed coupling introduces off-diagonal block feedforward, inflating the Kreiss constant: K(J multi ) ≥ K(J diag ). Consequently, the Kreiss-based conservative safe radius bound con- B ≤ r conservative (J diag ). For the exact safe shock tracts: r conservative (J multi ) ≡ ∥C∥ 2 e(2d)K(J multi ) ∗ radius r exact (J) ≡ B/M C (J), because all constituent blocks of J are entrywise non-negative t in the momentum economy, matrix powers J multi are entrywise non-decreasing in K 21 , yield- ∗ ∗ ing M C (J multi ) ≥ M C (J diag ) and exact radius contraction r exact (J multi ) ≤ r exact (J diag ). Coupled powers contain sums of leader-to-satellite propagation terms; their output magnitude depends 14 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets on the fixed loss coordinates. No market-calibrated contraction percentage is asserted. Proof. After ordering states by asset, the coupled matrix is block triangular with the same diagonal blocks as the decoupled direct sum. The diagonal compressions of its resolvent are unchanged. Its operator norm is therefore at least the maximum norm of those diagonal blocks, which is the decoupled resolvent norm; taking the Kreiss supremum gives the first inequality. Nonnegative powers and a nonnegative output operator are entrywise nonde- creasing in the directed coupling. The spectral norm is monotone for nonnegative matrices, giving M C (J multi ) ≥ M C (J diag ). The budget-radius inequalities follow with the same B and C. Proposition 2.8 demonstrates that multi-asset diversification does not automatically in- sulate liquidity providers from feedback fragility. On the contrary, asymmetric cross-impact networks (such as Bitcoin leading altcoins or large-cap equities driving ETFs) introduce feed- forward coupling that changes finite-time propagation in matrix powers J t , inflating peak transient loss M C and potentially reducing the radius under the stated assumptions. This is a conditional network result rather than a calibrated multi-asset estimate. 3 Data, Measurements, and the Observable Estimand 3.1 Observed Price Proxies and Flow The theoretical state x t = p t −p ∗ t is not observed in these datasets. For the primary Coinbase analysis we use p b = 10,000 log(P b ), where P b is the recorded bid–ask midpoint at the end of a 10-second bin, and an operational reference m b = (1 − α)m b−1 + αp b , α = 2/(300/10 + 1). The empirical state is x EMA = p b − m b . It is a deviation from a trailing filter, not a measured b fundamental pricing error. A separate robustness state is the raw return r b = p b − p b−1 . Signed executed flow f b is the recorded taker-buy minus taker-sell quote-currency notional aggregated in bin b. Repeated renders of the same book/trade record receive zero new flow following the recorded correction protocol. Price and flow both refer to information observed by the bin’s end. Existing source timestamps and rolling trade counters only provide the recorder’s timing resolution; they do not establish exchange-level execution latency. 15 Niroula and Niroula 3.2 From Human Markets to Machine Markets A Reduced-Form Diagnostic For an observable state v b ∈ {x EMA , r b } and observed flow f b , fit b     v v  b+1  = d + J  b  + e b+1 , f b+1 f b Q = J 12 J 21 , 1 − J 22 S = J 11 + Q. (37) Both regressors are observed at time b. The legacy implementation instead pairs v b with f b+1 , creating an overlapping forward-flow statistic. That alignment is retained only as a sensitivity comparison, not as a real-time observable state. Order-flow or price-unit rescaling conjugates J by a diagonal scaling matrix; the product J 12 J 21 , Q, S, and eigenvalues are unchanged. However, scale invariance does not establish causality, invariance to filtering, or equivalence to a latent economic state. Non-normal Euclidean norms additionally require fixed coordinates or a specified weighted norm. For J 11 , J 22 ∈ [0, 1) and J 12 J 21 ≥ 0, S < 1 characterizes the positive real-root bound- ary and Schur stability of this two-state fit. Outside those sign restrictions, S < 1 alone is insufficient; we always compute ρ(J) directly. A multivariate fit to raw returns is not interchangeable with a fit to a filtered price level. 3.3 Filters, Missingness, and Sessions For a martingale price with no price-to-flow feedback, the EMA deviation satisfies x EMA b+1 = +∆p b+1 ). Thus an anchor near 1−α = 0.93548 can arise mechanically. Positive (1−α)(x EMA b feedback must be interpreted against that construction and explicit no-adaptation controls. The revision excludes transitions crossing UTC dates, timestamp gaps, or equity session boundaries. It does not backward-fill missing prices or manufacture unobserved trading intervals. The primary crypto segments receive five EMA spans of initialization burn-in and require at least 500 retained observations. The equity analysis uses a separate rule: at least 600 raw session rows and a 500-event burn-in, so some retained equity fits are smaller than 500 observations. Segment estimates on the same date are combined using transition counts before date-level averaging and Student-t intervals. The 13 Coinbase calendar dates include partial first and last dates. These intervals summarize variation across observed dates; they do not provide a long-horizon or independent external replication guarantee. 3.4 Actual Dataset Scope Coinbase BTC, ETH, and ADA snapshots cover April 7–19, 2021. Binance’s 768 saved asset-day fits cover twice-monthly dates in 2021–2024, but their generator reads 1-second 16 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets trade-price klines and estimates at 10-second spacing with a 300-second EMA and forward flow. Klines do not contain bid–ask midpoints, queue identities, or full L3 books. The 66.3 million nominal seconds in the previous description are not the number of fitted transitions: the saved panel contains 6,519,552 fitted state rows, with one fewer transition per asset-day. Its original raw archives are not present in the inspected cache. FI-2010 is an event-based book benchmark (Ntakaris et al., 2018). The local representa- tion contains 272,941 rows with supplied STOCK and DAY fields. Those fields define this reanalysis; the original identifier mapping has not been independently authenticated. The January BTC depth file covers January 9–20, 2023 rather than the entire month. It contains quote depth, and the revision uses quote-update OFI, not authenticated executed trades. Its provider attribution is not independently established here. It was already examined before this revision, so it is a secondary sample rather than an untouched prospective holdout. 4 Observable Evidence and Fee Sensitivity 4.1 Fresh Coinbase Reanalysis The following table is generated from fresh end-bin-aligned fits of the existing corrected recorder data. This supports the importance of low-frequency flow exposure within the model; it prevents attributing the failure uniquely to adaptive learning or non-normal transients. The fixed-spectrum experiment above addresses transient magnification separately. The simulation does not measure actual dealer failures or demonstrate welfare benefits of an exchange gate. Historical flash-crash mitigation percentages are omitted from the main evidence because they were 25 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets calibrated illustrations rather than new causal event analyses. 6 Attribution, Falsification, and Replication Limits 6.1 Aggregate Relations Do Not Identify Algorithms The merged-cohort theorem concerns a stated linear, reset observation experiment. Anony- mous prices and flows cannot identify identities within a merged representation. More broadly, the empirical VAR here does not distinguish a learning algorithm from a persis- tent exogenous flow process or discretionary response to common news. Participant iden- tifiers improve disaggregation, but parameter recovery also requires a correct state model, sufficient regressor rank, and an orthogonality assumption; OLS alone is not an automatic causal identification guarantee. 6.2 What the Diagnostics Establish Timing comparisons show that the legacy and end-bin states differ. Raw-return checks show that filtered persistence is not interchangeable with return persistence. No-adaptation controls test a finite declared family, not every confounder. Covariance rejection remains unfavorable evidence about the low-dimensional approximation. Sign-memory adjustment is a descriptive robustness exercise, not proof of causal learning. The revision makes no blanket assertion that all placebo tests have passed or that common response proves propagation. 6.3 Traceability and Remaining Limits The revision archive records hashes, daily estimates, gap handling, inference calculations, numerical checks and source changes. Coinbase and equity calculations use existing local data representations; the January depth file is freshly streamed. Binance results are recomputed from saved derived estimates, not missing raw archives. No provider identity, immutable external preregistration, independent replication or expert mathematical review is certified by this internal audit. Where numerical provenance could not support the previous claim, the result was withdrawn rather than replaced by a preset favorable number. 26 Niroula and Niroula 7 From Human Markets to Machine Markets Conditional Surveillance Implications and Conclu- sion 7.1 Loss Budgets Require More Than Eigenvalues The exact radius is conditional on J, fixed state units, a declared shock set, a calibrated loss operator and budget B. If orders enter through a matrix G, the relevant immediate disturbance is z 0 = Gv; a scalar price-impact bound does not automatically bound the entire state. For repeated orders or innovations, z t = J z 0 + t t−1 X J t−1−k Gw k+1 , k=0 so an initial-shock radius alone is insufficient. A control design would require cumulative exposure bounds from inputs to outputs, and accounting for simultaneous portfolios and uncertain parameters. 7.2 A Conditional One-Burst Gate If a separately justified model gives ∥z 0 ∥ 2 ≤ g t V for a burst volume V , then V ≤ B t /(g t M C ) bounds the modeled loss from that burst. The loss budget B t must come from actual available capital and declared risk limits, not an unsupported multiplication of capital by leverage. Under C = I, B t /(enK(J)) is a conservative state-shock radius; an upper bound B t /K(J) must not be used as a guaranteed safe radius. For a general C, the factor ∥C∥ 2 enters a norm-based conservative bound. This mathematical implication does not establish that an exchange can observe every required input, run the estimator within its latency budget, improve price discovery, or prevent real insolvency. Comparing execution quality, delayed fills, liquidity and dealer outcomes against ordinary depth/size limits remains a separate prospective study. Circuit breakers and batching address additional market-design questions not resolved by these calculations. 7.3 Conclusion Observable price–flow data support model-dependent diagnostics, while participant attri- bution and financial guarantees require additional information and assumptions. Within the stated linear probing experiment, merged cohorts are observationally equivalent and symmetric close-rate alternatives have a fourth-order separation lower bound. The scalar 27 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets Gaussian price experiment supplies an explicit abstention layer near its unit-root boundary. The loss-budget identity shows why stable eigenvalues alone do not bound worst-case output magnification in fixed coordinates. Empirically, end-bin observed flow produces smaller Coinbase feedback diagnostics than legacy forward-flow timing; raw-return intervals span zero, and covariance restrictions are rejected. Saved Binance fee contrasts do not establish either a causal learning response or equivalence to zero. Separate fixed-spectrum and funded-dealer simulations distinguish transient magnification from persistent-flow accumulation, with exogenous long-run-variance matching reproducing severe model losses. These limits are part of the findings. The manuscript is a corrected internally audited working paper, with missing raw-panel repro- duction, independent review and real-market policy validation explicitly remaining open. 28 Niroula and Niroula A From Human Markets to Machine Markets Full Study Coverage and the Evidence Boundary This review revision retains all ten study questions and the information-contract and financial-risk program of the original 48-page manuscript. The original submission PDFs are preserved separately. Correcting an invalid result is different from abandoning its scientific question: the evidence below records successful reanalyses, model rejections, and specific missing dependencies. This version is a review candidate with open scientific gates, not a declaration of publication readiness. The page-disposition appendix connects every original page to its revision obligation. A.1 The Ten-Study Program Study 1: baseline aggregate diagnostics. The 768 asset-day archive answers a de- scriptive question about the fitted dynamics of a filtered price/flow proxy. Its matrices and derived invariants are internally consistent, but rechecking a stored matrix is not re- producing the transformation from exchange observations. The historical generator used close-price klines and forward-aligned flow. Accordingly, the archived means remain a sepa- rately labeled historical diagnostic. The primary observed-timing reanalysis on the traceable Coinbase sample shows how strongly the same scientific quantity changes under a corrected information convention. Study 2: cross-asset heterogeneity. Differences in the archived Q means across eight symbols can be reproduced from their saved fits. They do not identify institutional participa- tion or a monotone effect of capitalization, because no participant identities or independently aligned capitalization data enter these estimates. A study of heterogeneity remains useful when sampling, filtering and uncertainty are held fixed. The appendix reports the actual saved means rather than interpreting the rank ordering as a causal mechanism. Study 3: fee responsiveness. The saved 2022 panel permits reproduction of a treated- minus-control contrast around the fee change. Classical, asset-cluster and date-cluster uncer- tainty differ substantially. A one-treated-asset comparison needs a defensible counterfactual and assumptions about spillovers. A broad confidence interval containing zero does not es- tablish that fees leave feedback unchanged; the stated equivalence margin also fails under the reported date-cluster test. These are results of the intervention study, not reasons to exclude it. 29 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets Study 4: dynamics around the intervention. The twice-monthly dates identify de- scriptive contrasts relative to the last pre-treatment date. Recovering a date-specific point contrast does not recover its standard error. The inspected event-study generator assigns √ pooled DiD uncertainty scaled by 2, without estimating the covariance of the individual contrast, and its clock differs from the old monthly display. The original joint pretrend statistic is therefore not retained as verified evidence. The dated contrasts remain available below while inference assumptions are resolved. Study 5: venue transmission. A saved separate-venue comparison is evidence of differ- ences or similarities in marginal fitted dynamics. Transmission requires synchronized joint observations. The old displayed joint matrix contradicts its own spectral-radius claim, and a generating joint fit has not been established in the expanded artifact search. The research question remains open: estimate the joint process from a documented join, assess miss- ingness and clock conventions, and distinguish predictive lead–lag relations from identified information shocks. Study 6: forecast-error variance. FEVD additionally requires the residual covariance and a declared innovation identification or generalized decomposition. Percentages cannot be reconstructed from separate marginal summaries. Horizon labels must count the actual bin width: ten fitted steps at ten seconds per step do not represent ten seconds. Ordering sensitivity and the relation between quote midpoints and transaction-close proxies matter. No untraced percentage is offered as an observed systemic contribution in this revision. Study 7: liquidity-state dependence. The first-50,000-record controlled regression is a bounded diagnostic on a recorded sample, not a comprehensive nonlinear identification design. Its slope difference is not detected with HAC uncertainty, while residual scales differ modestly. The historical switching code fits a scalar differenced-EMA regression, uses ad hoc transition updates, and creates a dimensionally chosen index by multiplying a slope by ten. That index is not the structural S in the cohort theorem. A justified regime likelihood, initialization audit and uncertainty are required before a structural bifurcation conclusion. Study 8: historical stress scenarios. The inspected historical script simulates an E-mini path with imposed depth dynamics and assigns the reported feedback parameters directly. The Treasury routine returns fixed values. These outputs can motivate an illustrative stress scenario, but they are not estimates from ingested historical TAQ. Moreover, the protected E-mini scenario changes depth and external liquidation flow as well as the proposed intercep- 30 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets tion rule. Its improvement cannot isolate the rule’s causal effect. Authenticated historical observation, where recoverable, would be a separate empirical test. Study 9: the supplied equity sample. Session-reset fits reproduce aggregate diagnos- tics for supplied STOCK/DAY identifiers. Their counts differ across stocks, and their index is an event clock. The original benchmark/provider map has not been independently au- thenticated. The estimates therefore support replication of the local calculation, conditional on the supplied representation, rather than a fully authenticated cross-market mechanism. The session audit preserves actual stock counts and excludes cross-session transitions. Study 10: funded dealers. The 48-cell replay reproduces archived halt counts exactly under preserved flow-moment calibration. Matched independent and persistent-flow com- parators are important because inventory accumulation can arise without adaptive learning. Simulation seeds quantify path variability under that calibration; they are not independent market observations. The fixed-coordinate transient examples address a different determin- istic experiment. Keeping the two studies separate prevents a simulated halt percentage from being presented as a theorem or historical intervention outcome. A.2 Information Contracts and Their Distinct Scientific Roles Public observation, controlled aggregate probing and audited internal state provide different information. A public tape lacks participant identity and policy-state disclosures. An aggre- gate probe can excite a transfer function under its reset, observation-noise and admissible- input assumptions, but does not automatically separate equal-rate cohorts. Audited cohort- specific state/action histories can remove an aggregation ambiguity in the specified linear model. They cannot on their own establish a correct fundamental-value proxy, a stationary policy, or a calibrated balance-sheet loss mapping. A regression on disclosed state must specify whether the same-time price innovation enters the state update, which disturbances remain unobserved, and whether measurement error corrupts the disclosed variable. Ordinary least squares consistency cannot be inferred solely from observing a variable called “internal state.” Its moment restrictions need independent justification. Similarly, a Kalman recursion is an MMSE statement only under the stated distributional/independence model, and its steady-state gain concerns filtering error rather than financial solvency. An operational information contract would need an authenticated schema, timestamps, units, missingness policy and verification of access to the declared variables. The present analysis defines conceptual information requirements. It does not claim that a deployed 31 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets schema implements them or that firms’ supplied signals satisfy the model. Uncertainty sets for parameters and output exposures must precede a regulatory action based on a calculated radius. Aggregate model rejection is itself a reason to withhold a structural certification. B Repeated Innovations: A Conditional Loss Bound The initial-shock theorem does not control a stream of innovations. This gap has a direct conditional linear-system solution, stated here separately from empirical calibration. Proposition B.1 (Exact induced gain for bounded innovations). Each input independently maximizes its linear functional to r∥D ⊤ (J k ) ⊤ C ⊤ v∥ 2 , proving the finite-horizon equality. Taking the supremum over t proves P the formula. Schur stability implies summability of ∥J k ∥ 2 , so G ≤ k ∥CJ k D∥ 2 < ∞. For a scalar output, the dual sphere is {−1, 1} and the sum is independent of its sign. The initial-condition inequality follows from the triangle inequality and the definition of M C . P This result requires neither nonnegative coupling nor independence of the innovations. It controls bounded adversarial inputs in a fixed linear system; Gaussian innovations are unbounded and do not satisfy its almost-sure premise. A stochastic high-probability result needs a declared horizon and tail law. Applying the proposition to orders requires the actual input operator D, the economically calibrated loss operator C, fixed units and a justified parameter set. It does not establish market execution safety from a descriptive proxy VAR. For computation, let G N be the scalar-output partial sum through k = N − 1. Choose an integer h with q = ∥J h ∥ 2 < 1, which exists for a Schur-stable matrix. Commutativity of 32 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets powers and submultiplicativity give the tail certificate X ∥D∥ 2 h−1 0 ≤ G − G N ≤ ∥CJ N +j ∥ 2 . 1 − q j=0 Thus a truncated calculation can provide an interval for G rather than assuming that a finite horizon captured its maximum. Near instability the required horizon and uncertainty can be large. For a vector output, the partial dual optimization gives a lower bound and the summed operator norms give a conservative upper bound. C Measurement and Inference Methods C.1 The observable transformation The primary transformation forms past-observed bins, uses the last recorded midpoint in each bin and sums deduplicated executed signed flow. A missing bin splits the sequence; it is not filled from future values. The price state is log midpoint minus its exponential reference with α = 2/(W/∆ + 1). Five reference horizons are excluded after a segment reset. This changes both the estimand and its sample count. For raw-return diagnostics, differences are formed within the same contiguous segment. Daily aggregation treats multiple segments on one date as parts of one date, rather than independent observations. The observable proxy is not latent fundamental mispricing. Even a martingale filtered through an EMA produces memory. If a statement concerns fundamental stability, an observation-law relation is needed. Our reduced-form fit includes an intercept, and the off-diagonal ratio defining Q is a diagnostic of that fit. Dividing by 1 − J 22 can amplify uncertainty when flow persistence is close to one; the invariants must be read alongside the full fitted radius, sampling clock and denominator. C.2 Timing recovery The recovered Gemini scratch script independently compares one-minute reported buys against sums of one-second records under three interval closures. The deduplicated past interval reproduces every one of the tested 1,995 windows for each asset. The future interval does not. The corresponding duplicate-render counts are 79,581 (BTC), 73,762 (ETH), and 65,973 (ADA). These arithmetic checks support how to read the local flow timestamps; they do not authenticate the original provider or identify a trader’s policy. The revision also reconstructs each full local cache from its raw CSV with exact agreement. 33 Niroula and Niroula C.3 From Human Markets to Machine Markets Dependence and small samples Means and confidence intervals based on a daily panel describe variation across observed dates. They are not probabilities that an individual latent learning parameter falls in the displayed interval. For the saved Binance panel, all assets on a date are kept together in the date-block summary. The DiD covariance calculations state whether they use classical residual variance, eight asset clusters or twenty-four date clusters, with corresponding refer- ence degrees of freedom. Asset clustering with one treated asset remains fragile, even when the mechanical covariance calculation is correct. Eight assignment contrasts permit only a coarse descriptive rank fraction unless an ex- changeable assignment design is defended. The equivalence margin is a sensitivity choice, not a pre-registered economically optimal tolerance. Failing a TOST or failing to reject a zero effect cannot be combined into evidence that the effect is exactly zero. An event-specific covariance must be calculated for its own contrast, including uncertainty in the reference date. C.4 Minimum distance and rejection The reanalysis matches eleven covariance/lag moments to seven parameters and checks local rank seven. Segments contribute their own lagged products; products do not bridge dis- continuities. The fitted system is restricted to be stable and innovation covariance positive definite. The diagnostic uses HAC weighting with ten bins and a four-degree-of-freedom asymptotic reference. A successful optimizer supplies a candidate moment fit; rejection assesses the maintained moment model. It cannot establish structural validity through a nearby reduced-form point estimate. C.5 Null families and specification sensitivity The nulls are declared no-adaptation data-generating families, not fitted replicas of every feature of the real sample. They isolate independence, persistent exogenous flow, order splitting with impact, and common news. Sixty repetitions per family under the same transformation show that a small positive diagnostic is compatible with mechanisms other than adaptive learning. This is a bounded falsification exercise; a stronger mechanistic comparison needs calibrated information and uncertainty. The sampling/window grid is exploratory, and all admissible declared cells are retained. The W = ∆ = 60 cell is excluded because the chosen EMA becomes degenerate, not because its empirical result is unfavorable. 34 Niroula and Niroula From Human Markets to Machine Markets D Expanded Numerical Ledgers D.1 Saved cross-asset means The following numbers are means from the saved legacy panel. 0.0001101 0.975979 0.0000975 0.980657 0.0031508 0.907759 0.989067 0.983220 0.982063 0.980386 0.975981 0.980659 0.908027 Recovering Evidence Across Workspaces The search receipt indexes 14,804 text files and archive members, with 10,570 distinct content hashes. It includes related local release/repair folders, historical tar releases, a Zoom ZIP and Gemini/Antigravity scratch material. Texts larger than two megabytes, environments, credentials and Git objects were excluded from content matching. This is a bounded discov- ery search rather than a declaration that all possible backups have been read. Candidate text matches are reviewed semantically before they support a result. The recovered numeric-provenance matcher accepts a number if some token anywhere in a JSON/CSV rounds to it, including sign changes and factors of one hundred. Such a rule can accept an unrelated observation or simulated input and does not establish a generating chain. A source-to-data-to-estimator-to-field link is required instead. Agent completion reports and test counts are useful retrieval leads, but do not independently authenticate a historical sample or a theorem. Additional named data and release directories were listed on the external T9 volume, in- cluding January 2025 archives. After a temporary loss of access, the volume became readable and 458 research files were inventoried, including 192 data archives with matching checksum- file names. Small research JSON outputs were read and hashed; payload verification of all 192 archives is not asserted. The named binance-one-second directory contains no data files. The located archive dates and types do not establish the older one-second panel.
